lines.welcome.1: Ana and Omar tap Buy on the bakery's last croissant at the same moment. Both get a receipt.
lines.welcome.2: One croissant, two sales, and a database that said yes to both. By the end of this course, you'll know exactly why, and how to stop it.
lines.welcome.3: That's what this course is: how databases really work, from the inside, all the way up to what interviewers ask.
lines.welcome.4: No slides and no setup. You'll predict, write real SQL, and break things on purpose.
lines.welcome.interview: Then you're in the right place. Interviewers want the why, and you'll practise saying it out loud.
lines.welcome.design: Good. Replication, sharding and caching are all coming, and they stand on everything you build here first.
lines.welcome.curious: The best reason there is. You'll see what the machine actually does when you press Enter.
lines.welcome.5: Either way, we start small: a paper notebook and a pencil.
lines.story.1: The whole course follows one place, Maya's bakery, as it grows up.
lines.story.2: Level one: a paper notebook. You'll shape data so it stays correct, and ask it questions in SQL.
lines.story.3: Level two: the bakery goes online, on one server. You'll see how a database stores, finds and protects every order. That's where the croissant gets sold once.
lines.story.4: Level three: it becomes a chain, with many servers and a network that fails in creative ways. You'll scale out without losing data.
lines.story.5: Level four: a whole system grows around the database. Caches, event streams, analytics. You'll keep them all telling the same story.
lines.story.6: Level five is the deep end: electives on how specific database engines work.
lines.story.7: And every new idea arrives the way it does at work: as the bakery's next real problem.
lines.how.1: Every lesson plays like this one. I explain, and the pictures move with me.
lines.how.2: Then it's your turn. When the film stops, the next move is yours.
lines.how.3: At the end, an interviewer checks what stuck. It sounds like this.

how.interviewer.caption: Why can a query that returns twelve rows still read ten pages from disk?
how.interviewer.speaker: interviewer

lines.how.4: You'll be able to answer that very soon.
